thread:
maria (support): customer reporting intermittent 503s on hosted API this morning. they provided a request_id: abc123def456 and say it happened at approx 2024-09-03T10:15:00Z. asking for server-side log lookup and any quick repro tips.

jordan (infra): can you confirm which region/cluster and the endpoint they hit? prod-us-east? also need the exact request header set if they have it.

maria (support): they hit https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate in us-east, org=acme-co, user-provided header x-request-id: abc123def456. no extra debug bundle yet.

jordan (infra): doing a quick Kibana search would be: index: logs-prod-* AND (json.request_id: "abc123def456" OR trace.id: "abc123def456"). if you use KQL: request_id: "abc123def456" OR trace.id: "abc123def456". time range +- 5m around 2024-09-03T10:15:00Z.

jordan (infra): note: prod rolling indices keep logs for 15 days by default; if this is older it may be in the archive (s3://redwood-logs-prod/). for archives file a retrieval ticket — infra can help if you confirm the exact day.

maria (support): it's within 15d, so should be in the main index. can you run the query and paste any matching lines? customer says they saw 503 with body "upstream timeout".

jordan (infra): found two hits: (1) gateway proxy timeout -> upstream returned 503 after 30s; (2) model backend returned 502 then gateway converted to 503. snippets:
```
timestamp: 2024-09-03T10:14:59Z service: gateway severity: error msg: "upstream timeout" request_id: abc123def456 route: /v1/generate backend: model-pool-us-east-2 host: gpu-12
```
and
```
timestamp: 2024-09-03T10:15:01Z service: model-backend severity: warn msg: "backend error: connection reset" request_id: abc123def456 trace.id: trace-7f8e9
```

jordan (infra): attaching the raw JSON hits in the support thread. recommend collecting a debug bundle from the customer for full headers and prompt payload. debug bundle retains for 90 days.

maria (support): i'll request the debug bundle and send repro steps. any quick curl we can ask them to run to reproduce and capture response+headers?

samuel (eng-runtime): ask them to run a minimal curl that sets the same x-request-id and includes full body, e.g.:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "x-request-id: abc123def456" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
That will show upstream connect/reset and response headers. If they see TCP reset, include packet capture.

samuel (eng-runtime): also ask for the exact time they saw the 503 in their client; small clock skew matters when TTLs are tight.

maria (support): pinged customer for debug bundle + exact client timestamp. they sent back bundle id dbg-20240903-42 and client time 2024-09-03T10:14:59.

jordan (infra): grabbed the debug bundle, correlated with our logs: trace-7f8e9 shows repeated connection resets to host gpu-12 right around 10:15. escalated to eng-runtime to check gpu host health and kernel OOM possibility.

samuel (eng-runtime): confirmed backend had transient NIC flaps and restarted the process; we've applied a temporary routing fallback so new requests will route to gpu-14. we'll follow up with postmortem if recurrence.

maria (support): will update customer: explain transient infra failure, we've routed around it, ask them to retry and provide curl output if still failing. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident created INC-2024-5593 for infra follow-up and postmortem tracking.
